<thought>To determine the number of CH₃ groups, I will first obtain the 13C NMR spectrum of the sample (no arguments needed). Methyl carbons typically appear in the 10‑30 ppm region, so by counting distinct signals there I can infer the number of CH₃ groups. If the spectrum is ambiguous, I could later get the ¹H NMR, but the carbon spectrum should be sufficient and cheaper.</thought>
